summary: Armenia is visa-free for a broad range of passports — the EU, UK, US, Russia, Japan, the Gulf states and several other CIS and Latin American countries can stay up to 180 days in any one-year period, and China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uruguay up to 90 days — while most other nationalities can obtain an e-Visa online or a visa on arrival at Zvartnots Airport. A smaller group of nationalities must apply through an embassy with an invitation.

defaultStayWindow.text: The MFA states that citizens of countries with a visa-free regime “can stay on the territory of the Republic of Armenia for no more than 180 days during one year if no other term is defined by the international agreements”, and elsewhere on the same page puts the same allowance as 180 days “within any one-year period”. It is a rolling twelve months rather than a calendar year. The MFA does not say whether the days of arrival and departure are counted, so we count both.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Armenia — Visa

conditionalWaivers.text: From 1 July 2026 to 1 July 2027, nationals of 111 listed countries who hold a residence permit issued by the US, an EU or Schengen state, the UAE, Bahrain, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait or Oman, valid for at least six months from entry, can enter without a visa and stay up to 180 days in a year. The permit must be a physical card or a passport sticker showing, in Latin script, the document title, name, nationality, date of birth and validity dates.

safety.text: Armenia is generally safe with low crime, and Yerevan is comfortable to walk even late in the evening. Avoid the immediate border areas with Azerbaijan, where the situation can change quickly. Check current advice before visiting frontier regions.

bestTimeToVisit.text: The Government of Canada describes Armenia's climate as continental: in Yerevan summers are hot and winters mild, while much of the country lies above 1,000 m, where it is cooler and rainfall is more frequent. The rainy season generally runs from March to June and from October to November, when seasonal flooding can disrupt overland travel.

idp.text: Armenia is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: According to the UK Foreign Office, Armenia's land borders with Turkey and Azerbaijan are closed; the border with Iran is open to foreign nationals, though this can change at short notice. Overland you can otherwise enter from Georgia, or fly into Yerevan — there are direct flights from Istanbul.
The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel within 5 km of Armenia's entire eastern border with Azerbaijan, and along the M16/H26 road between Ijevan and Noyemberyan, because of border tensions.
The UK Foreign Office warns that hailing taxis on the street risks being scammed for high fares, and calls the GG taxi app a reputable service in Armenia.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Armenia?
faq.answer: Probably not. Citizens of the EU, UK, US, Russia, Japan, the Gulf states and several other CIS and Latin American countries enter visa-free and can stay up to 180 days in any one-year period; citizens of China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uruguay can stay up to 90 days. Most other nationalities can apply online for an e-Visa (21 or 120 days) or obtain a visa on arrival at Zvartnots Airport; some nationalities need an invitation and must apply through an embassy.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Armenia visa-free?
faq.answer: Most visa-waiver nationalities may stay up to 180 days in total within one year. Citizens of China, Iran, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uruguay get up to 90 days under their own agreements. Longer stays require a residence permit from the migration authorities.

faq.question: Can I get an Armenian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: For some nationalities. Around 20 — including Canada, Mexico, South Africa, Thailand and Türkiye — can get a visitor visa on arrival at Zvartnots Airport and open land crossings outright: AMD 3,000 for 21 days or AMD 15,000 for 120 days. Most other e-Visa nationalities qualify on arrival only if they hold a valid visa or residence permit from the EU or Schengen states, the US, the UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia or Japan, or a residence permit from a Gulf state; Taiwanese passports cannot get one. Applying online in advance at evisa.mfa.am works for all of them.

faq.question: Is the land border between Armenia and Turkey open?
faq.answer: No. According to the UK Foreign Office the land border with Turkey is closed, although there are scheduled direct flights between Yerevan and Istanbul, and the border with Azerbaijan is closed too. To combine Armenia and Turkey in one trip, fly or route overland through Georgia.
